# Project Dashboard v1.4.1

First GitHub release of the MIT-licensed Project Dashboard browser extension, including the Google account-selection repair.

## Fixed in 1.4.1

- Connect Google and Change account start an explicit account-selection flow instead of reusing a rejected cached token.
- Change account remains available after sign-in failures and cancellations.
- Rejected sessions, saved account hints and old-account cached rows are cleared without erasing the configured spreadsheet, tab names or OAuth client ID.
- Initial authentication waits for user selection; silent renewal is reserved for a previously selected account.

## Included

- A private Google Sheets-backed new-tab dashboard with configurable spreadsheet and tab names.
- In-extension daily/manual checks for the latest published stable GitHub release.
- Settings-only export/import, excluding access tokens and project rows.
- Windows in-place updater and GitHub release downloader with SHA-256 checking, remembered installation folder and recovery backup.
- Existing Project Pulse storage keys and installed configuration are preserved during in-place migration.
- No Chrome Web Store dependency, telemetry, remote executable JavaScript, or personal configuration in the distribution package.

## Upgrading an existing installation

Run `Update Project Dashboard.cmd` from the extracted package and select your existing extension directory when asked. The downloader checks the published release, validates its checksum and invokes the in-place upgrade helper. Do not uninstall the extension, load a second copy, move its existing directory or overwrite your local configuration manually.

After updating, select Reload on the same extension in `brave://extensions`, close older dashboard tabs and open a new tab. Click Change account to select the authorized Google account. The actual file installation runs through the Windows helper; the browser extension only detects and announces releases.

New installations: extract to a permanent folder, use Load unpacked on `extension/`, then configure your own private Sheet and OAuth client in Settings. No client secret belongs in the extension.

## Verification and known limitations

Automated JavaScript checks, package integrity tests, simulated Chromium UI/account-recovery tests, and Windows updater/download regression checks passed for the repair. The publishing workflow rebuilds the package, checks the pinned SHA-256, repeats source/package and Windows checks, and verifies the uploaded assets before publishing.

**Live Google OAuth and upgrade behavior in the user's real Brave profile have not been independently confirmed.** This release is published at the owner's request; publication is not a claim of full real-environment qualification. The Google/browser APIs used in UI tests were simulated. User-specific Sheet access and OAuth authorization must still be valid.

GitHub is the distribution channel. Chrome Web Store publication and fully automatic in-browser installation remain deferred. Packaged documentation retains the repair candidate's verification notes.
